literal: With the world to conform living, many things even after learning, those who have not learned are those who do not possess wisdom.
translation: Those who do not know how to live in harmony with the world are ignorant, even if they have learned many vast subjects.
modern: உலகத்தோடு பொருந்தி வாழக் கற்றுக் கொள்ளாதவர்கள், பல நூல்களைக் கற்றிருந்தாலும் அறிவு இல்லாத கல்லாதவர்களே ஆவர்.
explanation: This couplet emphasizes that practical social wisdom is far superior to mere academic learning. The phrase 'உலகத்தோடு ஒட்ட ஒழுகல்' means conducting oneself in harmony with the wise and noble people of the world. The poet asserts that even if a person has studied 'பல' (many) diverse subjects, they are still considered 'கல்லார்' (unlearned) and 'அறிவிலாதார்' (devoid of wisdom) if they lack the basic social grace to fit in with society. True education must reflect in one's behavior and ability to live peacefully among others.
